name: NICE CG95: Prolonged Acute Chest Pain (Suspected Acute Coronary Syndrome)
description: Adult presenting with acute chest pain lasting 20 minutes or longer requires emergency ambulance transfer.
section_number: Section 1.1.2: Presentation with acute chest pain

consequent.clinical_action: Emergency ambulance transfer (Call 112 / 108) to a hospital with emergency cardiac facilities. Do not transport by private vehicle.
consequent.clinical_rationale: Chest pain lasting >= 20 minutes at rest is a classical presentation of myocardial ischemia or acute myocardial infarction requiring rapid ECG and reperfusion.

name: NICE CG95: Acute Chest Pain Radiating to Arm/Jaw with Autonomic Symptoms
description: Acute chest pain radiating to left arm, neck, or jaw accompanied by diaphoresis or nausea.

consequent.clinical_action: Emergency blue-light ambulance transfer; keep patient resting and administer prescribed GTN if indicated by medical protocols.
consequent.clinical_rationale: The combination of radiation to the arm/jaw with diaphoresis markedly elevates likelihood ratios for acute myocardial infarction.

name: NICE CG95: Exertional Discomfort Relieved by Rest (Suspected Stable Angina)
description: Chest discomfort brought on by physical exertion and relieved within minutes by rest, without acute rest pain.
section_number: Section 1.2: People presenting with stable chest pain

consequent.clinical_action: Urgent primary care evaluation and referral to a rapid-access chest pain clinic within 1-2 weeks.
consequent.clinical_rationale: Classical features of stable angina warrant prompt diagnostic cardiology evaluation but do not indicate acute emergency myocardial necrosis.

name: EDUCATIONAL DEMO: Reproducible Musculoskeletal Chest Wall Tenderness
description: Demonstration rule: localized sharp chest wall pain fully reproduced by manual palpation, without dyspnea or cardiac risk features.
section_number: Section 1.3: Educational Demonstration - Musculoskeletal differential considerations

consequent.clinical_action: Routine primary care assessment for musculoskeletal chest pain / costochondritis with safety-net advice.
consequent.clinical_rationale: Educational rule demonstrating non-urgent triage classification for reproduced chest wall pain in the absence of red flags.
